title: AgentForge run.json
description: Persisted state for one /agentforge run. Written atomically after every stage transition so a run resumes from this file alone, with no transcript (FR-02). Decided in ADR-0001.

schema_version.description: Schema version this file was written against.

updated.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of the last write.

current_stage.description: GROUP 1 — active stage id, or null when the run is complete or escalated.

sprint_id.description: EP-08 (ADR-0005) — pointer to the cross-run sprint-NN.json container this run is enrolled in, set at S5. Optional per ADR-0001's migration rule: a pre-EP-08 run.json with no such key still loads, defaulting to null.

sequence.description: ADR-0022 D-3 — the named stage sequence this run walks: 'sdlc' (/agentforge, run_state.STAGE_SEQUENCE/STAGE_AGENTS) or 'ml' (/agentforge-ml, run_state.ML_STAGE_SEQUENCE/ML_STAGE_AGENTS). Optional and defaults to 'sdlc' so a pre-ADR-0022 run.json with no such key still loads unchanged.

completed_stages.description: GROUP 2 — stage ids that finished, in completion order. The resume cursor.

gate.description: GROUP 4 — gate/approval state. Reserved for the EP-02 HITL gates; not built in Phase 1.

escalation.description: Set when a stage fails twice consecutively (Task 32); null otherwise.

stages.description: Per-stage state, keyed by stage id — see run_state.STAGE_SEQUENCE for the full, current ordered list (S0 onboarding through the enablement stage).

agent.description: The agent (or, for command-only stages with no owning agent, a descriptive marker) that owns this stage — see run_state.STAGE_AGENTS for the current mapping.

status.description: Lifecycle. Written in_progress BEFORE the agent spawns, complete only AFTER it succeeds — so an interrupted stage reads in_progress on resume (FR-02).

consecutive_failures.description: Consecutive failed spawns for this stage; reset to 0 on success.

spawns.description: One record per agent spawn attempt on this stage.

spawned_by.description: Who initiated the spawn. The 'manual invocations = 0' metric counts non-orchestrator spawns (Task 34). 'external' (ADR-0012 EP-02, additive) is stamped by exchange/drive.py's apply_intent when an inbound Git-exchange drive intent advances a stage, so audit can tell an external driver apart from a human or the orchestrator; older run.json files with only 'orchestrator'/'human' still load unchanged.

identity.description: WHO proposed this spawn (ADR-0012 US-02-02, additive, optional — never required so an older run.json with no identity field still loads unchanged). Independent of spawned_by (WHICH category proposed it): an inbound drive intent's DriveIntent.identity is stamped here verbatim by exchange/drive.py's apply_intent for audit attribution, but is never trusted as an approval credential or used to derive spawned_by. '' (default) means unknown/not recorded, e.g. every orchestrator/human spawn that predates this field.

usage.description: GROUP 5 — per-run usage, aggregated into sprint-NN.json's runs accumulator by the PM-lane refresh() and read by /budget-report at S16 sprint-close. Figures are CUMULATIVE across every pass over the stage; individual passes are preserved in usage_history.

source.description: TD-018 provenance of the figures. AgentForge never observes tokens — the numbers are supplied by the caller — so the ledger records where each came from. 'measured': transcribed from a real reported usage figure. 'estimated': derived by a stated method (e.g. an orchestrator-owned stage, which has no spawn result to read). 'unrecorded': no figure available — NOT a zero, and excluded from rollup totals. 'unspecified': legacy/pre-TD-018 record, or figures supplied without declaring provenance.

usage_history.description: TD-018: one entry per superseded pass over this stage (a re-completion after reopen, or a retry after fail). Before this existed, re-completing a reopened stage OVERWROTE its usage and the prior pass's cost was lost — mirroring the spawn trail reopen_stage already preserves.
